decisions.reason: The approved Hero V is used as the reference for adjusting the lowercase v; its own geometry remains unchanged.
The source reiterates the existing rule that the É accent must be the literal Hero V terminal and match it exactly; it does not change the candidate's current derivation requirement.
The shared-terminal rule remains unchanged; the new state change concerns the lowercase v's restrained right-arm reach rather than the common terminal treatment.
The source addresses letterform geometry only and makes no decision about material or champagne-gold treatment.
The discussion of a custom identity is descriptive context; the source does not change the deferred internal-letterform construction requirement.
The source does not modify complete-wordmark kerning, rhythm, or visual hierarchy.
References to deliberateness and proprietary character are consistent with existing brand-expression goals but do not alter them.
The source refines elements within the wordmark and does not change the decision to use a wordmark-led identity without a separate icon or monogram.
